blurb: The first national public museum in the world, free since it opened in 1759, with about eight million objects from every continent.

facts.t: When the physician Hans Sloane died in 1753 he left 71,000 objects to the nation in return for £20,000 for his heirs. Parliament founded the museum to hold them, and it opened in 1759, free to all 'studious and curious persons'.

facts.h: Marx wrote Capital in the Reading Room
facts.t: The round Reading Room under the great dome opened in 1857. Karl Marx worked there for years on Das Kapital, and Gandhi, Lenin and Virginia Woolf held reader's tickets too.

Some of the most famous objects, like the Parthenon sculptures and the Benin Bronzes, were taken in ways many people now see as wrong, and Greece and Nigeria ask for them back. The museum's founding law limits what it can give away.
